note: Known deficit for tools/release/check_production_stream_defaults.py: 9 sites across 5 production files. Every entry is a production function or member that defaults its cudaStream_t to nullptr, which in a codebase whose compute and load streams are created with cudaStreamNonBlocking is a write whose ordering against the kernels that read it is unspecified. The mechanism, and why the fix is not being applied, are recorded speculatively. Tests are excluded on purpose: a defaulted stream in a test is correct, because nothing there races a compute stream. The count is by any parameter name, not only one called `stream` -- an earlier survey that matched only the name `stream` reported 32 and missed device.h's transfer_stream, device.cu's compute and load, and device.h's stream_. This pin is a ratchet, not a detector: it fails on ANY difference, so a count that grows is a regression and a count that shrinks is the upstream fix arriving and needing a deliberate, recorded update. Editing this file is the record of that decision. Updated 2026-09-29: upstream 064965c7 (refactor(kv): require explicit publication streams) removed the nullptr defaults from kv_store.h (5 sites) and paged_kv_cache.h (3 of 7), reducing the total from 36 to 28. Updated 2026-10-01: the FP8 TMA descriptor is now passed by value at alignas(64) on every platform, which deleted Fp8TmaDescriptorBlock entirely -- that struct held the file's only defaulted cudaStream_t (stream = nullptr), so the site is gone rather than moved. 28 to 27. Updated 2026-10-12: the upstream merge (81c8ce09..74671a4e) replaced struct DeviceExecutionView, whose `cudaStream_t stream = nullptr` was one of this file's four, with class CudaExecutionView -- a borrowed view whose stream has one owning source and no default. The site is gone rather than moved, so src/core/device.h goes 4 to 3 and the total 26 to 25. Updated 2026-10-13: the upstream merge (c996baa8) added `class CudaStream` to src/core/device.h, whose private `cudaStream_t stream_ = nullptr` is a fourth site in that file and takes the total 25 to 26. It is not the hazard this ratchet exists for, read in source at src/core/device.cu:193: the member has no setter and its only constructor calls cudaStreamCreateWithFlags(cudaStreamNonBlocking) and throws if that fails, so a constructed CudaStream never holds nullptr and cannot publish on the legacy stream. The site is recorded rather than removed because the pin is a count of the pattern, and the pattern is what a future edit to this class could turn back into the defect. Updated 2026-10-15: the stream-default ratchet now also sees upload.cpp's one site, which was already in the tree (introduced together with the PLE upload-slot machinery in the 2026-09 commit 5ac4d9f0 that separated disk preparation from upload slots). It shows up only now because the earlier gates (profile consistency, text encoding) masked it during the io-fix session. Recorded rather than removed, per precedent: UploadSlots::Impl::Slot::transfer and consumer default to nullptr as retirement and activation markers, with if(transfer)/if (consumer) guards in synchronize(), no setter, and assignment only in the live upload path. Same pattern and rationale as the 2026-10-13 CudaStream stream_ entry. Total 26 -> 27.
